compiled_state.description:
## Observation
Reported downstream (nava-rebar 0.13.1, Jira Cloud, S3 store; the ADP project). A bound local ticket that is deleted or archived classifies TERMINAL and binding_walk emits an outbound update {status: Done} on every pass. Reproduced on origin/main and v0.13.1 with the real classify/binding_walk (evidence: .rebar/worktrees/inv-bridge-tombstone/.rebar/scratch/inv-75058/, repro.py, out-main.txt, out-v0131.txt).

Intent on record: 444d-c21f-2c82-4622 (closed) states "Approved policy: local archive/delete drives the Jira issue to a terminal status (Done)", planned to "optionally retire the binding after the terminal transition", and its AC reads "drives that issue to ... Done, or unbinds it". Commit 4bd06245d66 built the transition and not the retirement, so the binding persists and re-closes a reopened Jira issue every pass. In ADP, 19 deleted stories are queued to close their Jira issues, held only by max_acting_fraction (19/130); ADP-41 was closed by one pass and later reopened by a person.

Gaps:
- binding_walk.py hardcodes `_TERMINAL_JIRA_STATUS = "Done"` instead of routing through effective_status_map(), contrary to 444d's implementation contract and docs/mapping-seam.md ("the reconciler routes each outbound status through the effective status map"); `archived` was never added to the map; a `deleted = "skip"` override has no effect.
- No supported way to retire a binding (BindingStore.unbind exists only internally; no CLI/library/MCP surface).
- `rebar delete`/`archive` give no warning that a bound ticket will close its Jira issue; undocumented.

## Decision (operator, 2026-10-30, option 1)
Keep closing the Jira issue by default when a bound local ticket is deleted or archived, then retire the binding once the close is confirmed. A `skip` mapping for `deleted` or `archived` retires the binding without touching Jira. No manual retire command (bindings are maintained automatically; users have no visibility into them). Per a later operator instruction, `rebar delete` and `rebar archive` behaviour and output stay unchanged: no bound-ticket warning in this ticket.

## Plan
1. Status-map routing. Add `"archived": "Done"` to `config.local_to_jira_status` and its parity twin `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`. Remove `binding_walk._TERMINAL_JIRA_STATUS`. For each off-snapshot binding the walk resolves the terminal target from `config.effective_status_map(<project key of the bound Jira key>, root=repo_root)` keyed by the local terminal status (`deleted` when status is deleted, otherwise `archived`); `run_differs` passes the resolver in. SKIP or an absent key yields no target.
2. Classify. `classify()` gains a keyword `terminal_target` (default "Done", so fsck and other callers keep today's verdicts). For a TERMINAL local with Jira PRESENT there is one branch: if `terminal_target` is None, or the Jira status equals the target, or the Jira status is in `_JIRA_TERMINAL_STATUSES`, return a new `DecisionKind.RETIRE_TERMINAL` (reason names which); otherwise TERMINAL_TRANSITION with the target in its payload. The existing early NOOP return for an already-terminal Jira status (classify.py, "steady state") is removed, not kept beside the new branch. RETIRE_TERMINAL joins ACTING_KINDS, so mass retirement stays under the existing `max_acting_fraction` breaker exactly like RETIRE_AFTER_GRACE.
3. Binding walk. TERMINAL_TRANSITION emits `{status: <target>}` from the decision payload. RETIRE_TERMINAL retires the binding through the existing soft-delete (`BindingLifecycle.retire`, RETIRED FIRST; new `BindingStore.retire_terminal` facade) with the retired entry recording `reason: "local_terminal"`; nothing is written when `persist=False`. Confirmation is level-triggered: a pass that closes the issue leaves the binding, and the next pass that observes the target (or another terminal) status retires it. A retired key is never re-adopted (existing SKIP_RETIRED) and is no longer re-closed after a human reopens it.
4. Suppressed-create alert text. If a retired local ticket later becomes active again (an undone archive), the existing create suppression fires; its reason names the retire cause from the retired entry (local terminal vs confirmed 404) instead of always claiming a 404.
5. Docs. docs/mapping-seam.md: terminal transitions route through `effective_status_map`, `archived` added, `deleted`/`archived` = `skip` retires without a Jira write. docs/jira-sync-setup.md: a bound ticket deleted or archived closes its Jira issue and is then unbound; changing a ticket type locally never retypes an existing Jira issue, and deleting a ticket to recreate it as another type closes the original issue and creates a duplicate.
6. Tests first: tests/unit/reconciler/classify/test_matrix.py, tests/unit/reconciler/test_binding_walk.py, tests/unit/reconciler/test_status_mapping.py; update tests/unit/reconciler/classify/test_frozen_census.py so its simulated heal ends with the terminal bindings retired (zero drift preserved).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] With no `[mapping]` block, a bound deleted ticket whose Jira issue is To Do yields one outbound update `{status: "Done"}` and the binding stays live.
- [x] A bound archived ticket's transition target comes from `effective_status_map`; a project override `archived = "Cancelled"` yields `{status: "Cancelled"}`.
- [x] A pass that observes the bound issue already at its target status retires the binding to bindings-retired.json with `reason: "local_terminal"` and emits no Jira mutation.
- [x] A bound deleted ticket whose Jira issue is already Cancelled while the target is Done classifies RETIRE_TERMINAL, not NOOP and not TERMINAL_TRANSITION.
- [x] With `deleted = "skip"`, a bound deleted ticket whose Jira issue is To Do produces no Jira mutation and its binding is retired.
- [x] After retirement, a Jira issue reopened to To Do produces no mutation and is not adopted.
- [x] RETIRE_TERMINAL counts toward the breaker: 14 retirements over 130 bindings at `max_acting_fraction` 0.1 are refused with no binding retired.
- [x] `persist=False` (preview) retires nothing.
- [x] `bridge fsck` verdicts are unchanged (held-out oracle and last-synced tests pass unmodified).
- [x] The create-suppressed alert for a locally re-activated, terminal-retired ticket names the local-terminal cause.
- [x] docs/mapping-seam.md and docs/jira-sync-setup.md describe routing, skip-retire, and the type-change hazard.

## Non-goals
`rebar delete`/`archive` changes; a manual retire/unbind surface; retiring on applier success in the same pass; fsck awareness of project status maps (fsck keeps the default Done target); new handling for a Jira workflow that rejects the transition (the applier's existing per-mutation failure reporting and the breaker are unchanged).
